108:   <div class="callout">
109:     <div class="callout-title">How to use this document:</div>
110:     <p>Work through each section during the heuristic walkthrough. For each item, check it off when evaluated and record observations below the section. Rate severity:</p>
111:     <div class="severity-row">
112:       <div class="severity-item"><div class="severity-dot dot-green"></div> Holding up well</div>
113:       <div class="severity-item"><div class="severity-dot dot-yellow"></div> Opportunity</div>
114:       <div class="severity-item"><div class="severity-dot dot-red"></div> Significant gap</div>
115:     </div>
116:     <p class="callout-note">Not every item will apply to every product — use judgment. The goal is a rich findings list, not a complete score. Code scan data (hardcoded values, token mapping) is appended at the end.</p>
117:   </div>
118:
119:   <div class="exec-summary">
120:     <div class="exec-title">Executive Summary</div>
121:     <div class="stat-row">
122:       <div class="stat-box">
123:         <div class="stat-num">441</div>
124:         <div class="stat-label">Hardcoded color refs</div>
125:       </div>
126:       <div class="stat-box">
127:         <div class="stat-num">7</div>
128:         <div class="stat-label">WCAG contrast risks</div>
129:       </div>
130:       <div class="stat-box">
131:         <div class="stat-num">32</div>
132:         <div class="stat-label">Total findings</div>
133:       </div>
134:       <div class="stat-box">
135:         <div class="stat-num">24/52</div>
136:         <div class="stat-label">Colors exact-match tokens</div>
137:       </div>
138:     </div>
139:     <div class="exec-verdict">The BetaNXT Issuer Portal is a mature, MUI-based application with a solid design system foundation (@rolemodel/betanxt-design-system). The architecture is sound — CSS variables are used correctly in stylesheets, MUI components are well-customized, and there's a shared EmptyState, SkeletonTable, and Snackbar pattern. The single most important recommendation is to eliminate the 10 instances of native `alert()` calls and replace them with MUI Snackbar/toast patterns, as these block the main thread and provide no accessibility hooks. The effort to migrate hardcoded colors in PDF export utilities and the signature-maker.css to design tokens is moderate (~2-3 days) and would significantly improve maintainability.</div>
140:   </div>
141:
142:   <!-- SECTION 1 -->
143:   <div class="section">
144:     <div class="section-header">
145:       <h2 class="section-title">Section 1: First Impressions &amp; Visual Coherence</h2>
146:     </div>
147:     <p class="section-intro">What a user feels in the first 30 seconds — and whether the product looks and feels like one thing.</p>
148:     <div class="checklist">
149:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Does the product make a strong first impression? Is the purpose immediately clear? Does it feel trustworthy and intentional?</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>Aesthetic-Usability Effect: Users perceive aesthetically pleasing design as more usable.</p></div><div class="check-finding opportunity">[S1-1] <strong>Opportunity.</strong> 76 unique hardcoded hex colors across 25+ files create visual drift. MUI-based architecture is solid, but PDF export utilities and signature-maker.css use colors disconnected from the theme system. (P)</div></div>
150:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Is the visual language consistent throughout? Check button styles, typography, color usage, spacing, and iconography across multiple screens.</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>Law of Similarity / Law of Uniform Connectedness: Inconsistent visual treatment signals inconsistent relationships.</p></div><div class="check-finding gap">[S1-2] <strong>Gap.</strong> #EBB322 hardcoded in StatusChip.tsx:189 instead of using var(--mui-palette-gold-500). signature-maker.css uses #053f5a, #D3D3D3, #000 hardcoded — all have exact token equivalents. 58 hardcoded pixel values in inline styles. (H)</div></div>
151:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Does the brand come through clearly?</label></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S1-3] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> Multi-tenant brand system with 50+ client configs in brandConfig.ts. createClientTheme() properly merges brand colors with base theme. ClientAppSwitcher enables cross-client navigation. (Pass)</div></div>
152:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Is there visual hierarchy on key screens?</label></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S1-4] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> MUI typography scale managed by betanxt-design-system. Only 10 hardcoded font-size values, all in PDF exports — not in the main UI. Phase-based layout system provides clear content hierarchy. (Pass)</div></div>
153:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Is the color system doing meaningful work?</label></div><div class="check-finding opportunity">[S1-5] <strong>Opportunity.</strong> MUI CSS variables used correctly in stylesheets (var(--mui-palette-*), var(--mui-shadows-*)). But 441 total hardcoded color references undermine the system. 24 of 52 unique colors have exact token matches available. (P)</div></div>
154:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Does the typography scale feel intentional?</label></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S1-6] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> baseTypography imported from betanxt-design-system/themes/base/typography. dataCell, dataHeader, caption variants defined in theme overrides. No arbitrary font-size values in the main UI. (Pass)</div></div>
155:     </div>
156:     <span class="observations-label">Observations:</span>
157:     <div class="observations-area">[S1-1] <strong>Hardcoded color drift across components.</strong> 76 unique hardcoded hex colors found across 25+ files. While many are in the dynamic brandConfig.ts (expected for multi-tenant branding), significant drift exists in PDF export utilities, StatusChip (#EBB322 hardcoded at issuer-portal/components/ui/StatusChip.tsx:189), and signature-maker.css (#053f5a, #D3D3D3). (P)
158: [S1-2] <strong>Typography scale is MUI-managed — good.</strong> The design system provides typography via baseTypography from betanxt-design-system. Only 10 hardcoded font-size values found, all in PDF export utilities and signature-maker.css, not in the main UI. (Holding up well)
159: [S1-3] <strong>Brand system is multi-tenant by design.</strong> 50+ client brand configs in brandConfig.ts with dynamic primaryColor/secondaryColor. This is intentional architecture, not a drift issue. Theme creation via createClientTheme() properly merges brand colors with the base theme. (Holding up well)</div>
160:   </div>
161:
162:   <!-- SECTION 2 -->
163:   <div class="section">
164:     <div class="section-header">
165:       <h2 class="section-title">Section 2: Navigation &amp; Wayfinding</h2>
166:     </div>
167:     <p class="section-intro">Can users find what they need, understand where they are, and get back if they get lost?</p>
168:     <div class="checklist">
169:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Is the navigation structure predictable?</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>Jakob's Law: Users expect your product to work like others they know.</p></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S2-1] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> EventTabs provides scrollable meeting navigation with aria-labeled arrows. AppBar follows standard web conventions with logo, tabs, notifications, and profile. PhaseDrawer organizes content by workflow stage. (Pass)</div></div>
170:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Do users always know where they are?</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>Users shouldn't have to remember where they are.</p></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S2-2] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> PageTitle.tsx includes breadcrumb navigation with aria-label="breadcrumb". PhaseDrawer shows current phase number. EventTabs highlight active meeting. (Pass)</div></div>
171:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Are navigation labels clear and in plain language?</label></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S2-3] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> Navigation labels use plain language: "Scroll meetings left/right", "Add new task", "Share calendar", "Enter fullscreen". No internal jargon detected in aria-labels. (Pass)</div></div>
172:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Is the depth of navigation appropriate?</label></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S2-4] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> Route structure: /[clientTicker]/meeting/[meetingId]/[section] — 3 levels max. PhaseDrawer provides in-context navigation within meetings. Most content reachable in ≤3 clicks. (Pass)</div></div>
173:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Does the navigation work on mobile?</label></div><div class="check-finding opportunity">[S2-5] <strong>Opportunity.</strong> useMediaQuery(theme.breakpoints.down('md')) used in EventTabs, PhaseDrawer, MonthView, NumberCounter. But no skip-nav link means mobile keyboard users must tab through full AppBar. (M)</div></div>
174:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Are there dead ends?</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>Users need a clearly marked "emergency exit".</p></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S2-6] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> EmptyState component used in 10+ locations with clear CTAs. Dialogs have close buttons with aria-label. PhaseDrawer has "Close upload view and return to overview" button. (Pass)</div></div>
175:     </div>
176:     <span class="observations-label">Observations:</span>
177:     <div class="observations-area">[S2-1] <strong>EventTabs provides meeting navigation with scroll arrows.</strong> EventTabs.tsx implements left/right scroll buttons with aria-labels ("Scroll meetings left/right"). The component uses useMediaQuery for mobile detection at md breakpoint. (Holding up well)
178: [S2-2] <strong>PageTitle includes breadcrumb navigation.</strong> PageTitle.tsx has aria-label="breadcrumb", providing wayfinding context. (Holding up well)
179: [S2-3] <strong>ClientAppSwitcher enables cross-client navigation.</strong> The AppBar includes a ClientAppSwitcher component with role="complementary" at issuer-portal/components/Navigation/AppBar.tsx:160. (Holding up well)
180: [S2-4] <strong>Phase-based drawer navigation.</strong> PhaseDrawer uses useMediaQuery for mobile (md breakpoint) and provides phase-based content organization with aria-label="Loading phase data" and role="region" for each phase. (Holding up well)</div>
181:   </div>
182:
183:   <!-- SECTION 3 -->
184:   <div class="section">
185:     <div class="section-header">
186:       <h2 class="section-title">Section 3: Cognitive Load &amp; Complexity</h2>
187:     </div>
188:     <p class="section-intro">How hard is the product making users think?</p>
189:     <div class="checklist">
190:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Are screens trying to do too much?</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>Hick's Law / Miller's Law: Decision time increases with complexity.</p></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S3-1] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> Phase-based workflow breaks complex meeting management into digestible stages. PhaseDrawer organizes content by workflow step. SkeletonTable used consistently to reduce visual load during loading. (Pass)</div></div>
191:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Is information chunked effectively?</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>Law of Common Region / Proximity: Grouping reduces cognitive effort.</p></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S3-2] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> Card-based layout (MUI Card) groups related information. MeetingInformationCard, VotingSharesCard, MeetingRolesCard each handle one concern. Tabulation uses separate tables for proposals and positions. (Pass)</div></div>
192:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Are forms as simple as they can be?</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>Occam's Razor: Every extra field is a cost to the user.</p></div><div class="check-finding opportunity">[S3-3] <strong>Opportunity.</strong> FileUploadDialog has clear flow but no field-level validation feedback visible in code. Form utilities (planFileRequestForm, transferAgentRequestForm) use hardcoded colors (#969696, #C8C8C8, #F0F0F0) suggesting custom form styling outside MUI. (M)</div></div>
193:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Does the UI surface meaningful defaults?</label></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S3-4] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> EmptyState provides default content when no data exists. SkeletonTable shows structural placeholder during loading. MUI components have sensible defaults (elevation, spacing, typography). (Pass)</div></div>
194:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Is the language plain and direct?</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>Speak the user's language, not the system's.</p></div><div class="check-finding opportunity">[S3-5] <strong>Opportunity.</strong> Error messages in alert() calls are human-readable ("Failed to download document. Please try again.") but the alert() pattern itself is jarring. TabulationReportCard uses "Unable to generate report. Meeting data is not available." — clear but could suggest next steps. (M)</div></div>
195:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Are there progress indicators for multi-step processes?</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>Goal-Gradient Effect / Zeigarnik Effect.</p></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S3-6] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> PhaseDrawer with phase-based progress. LinearProgress with custom phase colors (theme.ts:703-756). Meeting phases clearly numbered and labeled. CircularProgress used for async operations. (Pass)</div></div>
196:     </div>
197:     <span class="observations-label">Observations:</span>
198:     <div class="observations-area">[S3-1] <strong>Phase-based progress system.</strong> The PhaseDrawer and PhaseContext provide a structured multi-step workflow with progress tracking. LinearProgress supports custom phase colors via CSS variables (theme.ts:703-756). (Holding up well)
199: [S3-2] <strong>Skeleton loading states reduce perceived complexity.</strong> SkeletonTable is used consistently across DocumentsSection, VotingTabulationTable, QuorumPerformanceTable, and PastMeetingsTable. ChartSkeleton used on reporting pages. (Holding up well)
200: [S3-3] <strong>EmptyState component used consistently.</strong> Found in 10+ locations including reports, meetings, documents, guests, agenda, and digital shareholder meeting pages. Provides consistent empty-state UX. (Holding up well)</div>
201:   </div>
202:
203:   <!-- SECTION 4 -->
204:   <div class="section">
205:     <div class="section-header">
206:       <h2 class="section-title">Section 4: Key Flows &amp; Task Completion</h2>
207:     </div>
208:     <p class="section-intro">Walk through the most critical user journeys.</p>
209:     <div class="tasks-block">
210:       <p>Core tasks being evaluated:</p>
211:       Review and manage meeting documents (upload, view, comment)<br>
212:       Track voting tabulation and generate reports<br>
213:       Manage meeting phases and timelines
214:     </div>
215:     <div class="checklist">
216:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Is the entry point obvious?</label></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S4-1] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> EventTabs provide clear meeting navigation entry. PhaseDrawer shows available phases with content. DocumentsSection has clear upload button. (Pass)</div></div>
217:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Are calls to action clear and appropriately sized?</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>Fitts's Law: Target size and distance affect accuracy.</p></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S4-2] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> MUI Button component used throughout with variant hierarchy (contained > outlined > text). FileUploadDialog has clear submit button with loading state. Export buttons use MUI Button with dropdown menus. (Pass)</div></div>
218:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Does the flow match the user's mental model?</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>When product structure doesn't match user thinking, errors increase.</p></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S4-3] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> Phase-based workflow mirrors real meeting planning process (setup → documents → mailing → voting → tabulation → reporting). MeetingInformationCard, DocumentsSection, VotingTabulation follow natural meeting lifecycle. (Pass)</div></div>
219:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Are there unnecessary interruptions or confirmation steps?</label></div><div class="check-finding gap">[S4-4] <strong>Gap.</strong> No confirmation dialogs found for delete operations. SecureFileTransferTable has "Delete file" button with no visible confirmation step. VotingSharesCard has alert(`Confirm action for ${label}`) at line 37 — a placeholder, not a real confirmation. (H)</div></div>
220:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Are error states handled gracefully?</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>Error messages should be plain language, identify the problem, suggest a solution.</p></div><div class="check-finding gap">[S4-5] <strong>Gap.</strong> 10 native alert() calls across the codebase: DocumentViewer.tsx (4), TabulationReportCard.tsx (1), DocumentSiteCard.tsx (1), DSMParticipants.tsx (1), broadridgeFormHandler.tsx (1), VotingSharesCard.tsx (1), TaskActions.tsx (1). These are modal-blocking, non-dismissable by Escape, and provide no accessibility hooks. (C) — replace with MUI Snackbar.</div></div>
221:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Does the product handle edge cases?</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>Postel's Law: Gracefully handle unexpected input.</p></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S4-6] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> EmptyState component used in 10+ locations. SkeletonTable for loading states. Error boundaries in PDF viewer (DocumentViewer.tsx:260). Form validation in FileUploadDialog. (Pass)</div></div>
222:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">What is the peak moment and ending of each flow?</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>Peak-End Rule: Users judge by the most intense moment and the end.</p></div><div class="check-finding opportunity">[S4-7] <strong>Opportunity.</strong> File upload flow ends with "Submit" button changing to "Uploading..." — good feedback. But success confirmation uses alert() instead of a celebratory Snackbar. Document download errors end with alert("Failed to download document. Please try again.") — functional but not reassuring. (M)</div></div>
223:     </div>
224:     <span class="observations-label">Observations:</span>
225:     <div class="observations-area">[S4-1] <strong>Native alert() calls block task flows.</strong> Found 10 instances of native `alert()` across the codebase: DocumentViewer.tsx (4), TabulationReportCard.tsx (1), DocumentSiteCard.tsx (1), DSMParticipants.tsx (1), broadridgeFormHandler.tsx (1), VotingSharesCard.tsx (1), TaskActions.tsx (1). These are modal-blocking, non-dismissable by keyboard escape, and provide no accessibility hooks. (C) — replace with MUI Snackbar.
226: [S4-2] <strong>FileUploadDialog provides clear upload flow.</strong> FileUploadDialog.tsx has proper disabled states during upload, clear submit button text changes ("Uploading..." vs "Submit"), and a close button with aria-label. (Holding up well)
227: [S4-3] <strong>DocumentViewer has download error handling.</strong> Multiple alert() calls for download failures (DocumentViewer.tsx:954, 987, 1009, 1107) — see S4-1. The error messages are human-readable but use the wrong pattern.</div>
228:   </div>
229:
230:   <!-- SECTION 5 -->
231:   <div class="section">
232:     <div class="section-header">
233:       <h2 class="section-title">Section 5: Feedback &amp; System Communication</h2>
234:     </div>
235:     <p class="section-intro">Does the product keep users informed and in control?</p>
236:     <div class="checklist">
237:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Does the product acknowledge user actions?</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>Visibility of System Status / Doherty Threshold.</p></div><div class="check-finding gap">[S5-1] <strong>Gap.</strong> PhaseDrawer has snackbar (snackbarMessage, snackbarOpen at PhaseDrawer.tsx:201-202) but DocumentViewer and other components use alert() instead. Inconsistent feedback patterns mean users get different responses depending on which flow they're in. (H)</div></div>
238:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Are loading states handled?</label></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S5-2] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> 476 loading-related matches. CircularProgress in PDF viewer, SkeletonTable for data tables, LoadingButton for form submissions. Suspense boundaries on reporting pages with ChartSkeleton fallback. Dynamic imports for heavy components (PDF viewer, video player). (Pass)</div></div>
239:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Are success and error states distinct and clear?</label></div><div class="check-finding opportunity">[S5-3] <strong>Opportunity.</strong> Error states use alert() (red flag pattern) while success uses snackbar in PhaseDrawer. No visual distinction between error types — all alerts look the same to the user. Should use MUI Alert with severity prop (error, warning, info, success). (M)</div></div>
240:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Is the undo/back behavior predictable?</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>User control and freedom.</p></div><div class="check-finding gap">[S5-4] <strong>Gap.</strong> No undo pattern detected. 197:       justify-content: space-between;
198:       align-items: flex-end;
199:     }
200:
201:     .cover-footer .logo-white svg { height: 36px; width: auto; }
202:
203:     .cover-meta {
204:       font-family: 'Geist Mono', monospace;
205:       font-size: 11px;
206:       color: rgba(255,255,255,0.5);
207:       text-align: right;
208:       line-height: 1.5;
209:     }
210:
211:     /* Tri-color accent bar at bottom of cover */
212:     .cover-accent-bar {
213:       width: 100%;
214:       height: 3px;
215:       margin-top: 16px;
216:       background: linear-gradient(90deg,
217:         var(--rm-blue) 0%, var(--rm-blue) 33%,
218:         var(--orange) 33%, var(--orange) 66%,
219:         var(--light-blue) 66%, var(--light-blue) 100%);
220:       border-radius: 2px;
221:     }
222:
223:     /* ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
224:        INTERIOR TYPOGRAPHY
225:        Canonical heading system (H1 through H6). Uses semantic heading
226:        elements wrapped for H1 and H2 so numeric ornaments compose with
227:        the heading word.
228:
229:        H1: overlapping ghost watermark numeral behind RM Blue title
230:        H2: Geist Mono kicker number tight above, RM Blue title,
231:            short RM Blue accent bar; leading paragraph has extra margin
232:            so the bar reads as equidistant between heading and body
233:        H3: Dark Blue Green title with thin N1 underline, no numbering
234:        H4: bold N8
235:        H5: small-caps Geist Mono N8
236:        H6: italic N6
237:        ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */
238:
239:     /* H1: watermark behind title, no accent bar */
240:     .h1-wrap {
241:       position: relative;
242:       padding-top: 22px;
243:       margin: 40px 0 20px 0;
244:       overflow: visible;
245:       break-before: page;
246:       break-after: avoid;
247:     }
248:     .h1-wrap.first { break-before: auto; margin-top: 0; }
249:     .h1-wrap .watermark {
250:       position: absolute;
251:       top: -8px; left: -8px;
252:       font-weight: 800; font-size: 120px; line-height: 0.85;
253:       color: #EDEDED;
254:       letter-spacing: -4px;
255:       pointer-events: none; user-select: none;
256:       z-index: 0;
257:     }
258:     .h1-wrap h1 {
259:       position: relative; z-index: 1;
260:       font-size: 42px; font-weight: 700;
261:       letter-spacing: -1.2px; color: var(--rm-blue);
262:       line-height: 1.05;
263:       padding-top: 26px;
264:     }
265:
266:     /* H2: kicker + title + accent bar stacked as one unit */
267:     .h2-wrap {
268:       margin-top: 32px;
269:       break-after: avoid;
270:     }
271:     .h2-wrap .kicker {
272:       display: block;
273:       font-family: 'Geist Mono', monospace; font-size: 11px;
274:       font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase;
275:       color: var(--n5);
276:       line-height: 1;
277:       margin-bottom: 2px;
278:     }
279:     .h2-wrap h2 {
280:       font-size: 24px; font-weight: 700;
281:       letter-spacing: -0.6px; color: var(--rm-blue);
282:       line-height: 1.15;
283:     }
284:     .h2-wrap .bar {
285:       width: 40px; height: 2.5px; background: var(--rm-blue);
286:       margin-top: 3px; border-radius: 1px;
287:     }
288:     .h2-wrap + p,
289:     .h2-wrap + .body-text { margin-top: 14px; }
290:
291:     .body-text {
292:       font-size: 15px;
293:       line-height: 1.75;
294:       color: var(--text);
295:       margin-bottom: 18px;
296:     }
297:
298:     .body-text + .body-text { margin-top: 0; }
299:
300:     /* Unordered list (canonical): filled RM Blue square at level 1,
301:        then filled circles for levels 2 and 3 (Dark Blue Green, then
302:        neutral) so the marker shape softens as depth increases.
303:        Bullets are indented from the paragraph edge so they read as a
304:        distinct block rather than flush body text. */
305:     .body-text ul, ul.body-list {
306:       margin: 10px 0 18px 28px;
307:       padding: 0;
308:       list-style: none;
309:       font-size: 15px;
310:       line-height: 1.75;
311:     }
312:     .body-text ul li, ul.body-list li {
313:       padding-left: 22px;
314:       position: relative;
315:       margin-bottom: 8px;
316:     }
317:     .body-text ul li > ul, ul.body-list li > ul {
318:       margin-top: 6px;
319:       margin-left: 4px;
320:       padding-left: 0;
321:     }
322:     .body-text > ul > li::before, ul.body-list > li::before {
323:       content: '';
324:       position: absolute;
325:       left: 0;
326:       top: 9px;
327:       width: 6px;
328:       height: 6px;
329:       background: var(--rm-blue);
330:       border-radius: 1.5px;
331:     }
332:     .body-text ul ul > li, ul.body-list ul > li {
333:       padding-left: 16px;
334:     }
335:     .body-text ul ul > li::before, ul.body-list ul > li::before {
336:       content: '';
337:       position: absolute;
338:       left: 0;
339:       top: 7px;
340:       width: 6px;
341:       height: 6px;
342:       border: 1.2px solid var(--dark-blue-green);
343:       border-radius: 1px;
344:       background: transparent;
345:     }
346:     .body-text ul ul ul > li, ul.body-list ul ul > li {
347:       padding-left: 14px;
348:     }
349:     .body-text ul ul ul > li::before, ul.body-list ul ul > li::before {
350:       content: '';
351:       position: absolute;
352:       left: 0;
353:       top: 7px;
354:       width: 5px;
355:       height: 5px;
356:       border: 1px solid var(--n5);
357:       border-radius: 1px;
358:       background: transparent;
359:     }
360:
361:     .body-text a {
362:       color: var(--rm-blue);
363:       text-decoration: underline;
364:     }
365:
366:     .body-text strong { font-weight: 700; }
367:
368:     /* H3: thin underline, no numbering */
369:     h3 {
370:       font-size: 17px; font-weight: 700;
371:       letter-spacing: -0.25px; color: var(--dark-blue-green);
372:       margin-top: 14px; margin-bottom: 4px;
373:       display: inline-block;
374:       border-bottom: 2px solid var(--n1);
375:       padding-bottom: 1px;
376:       break-after: avoid;
377:     }
378:
379:     /* H4-H6: no numbering, type-only hierarchy */
380:     h4 {
381:       font-size: 14px; font-weight: 700;
382:       letter-spacing: -0.1px; color: var(--n8);
383:       margin-top: 16px; break-after: avoid;
384:     }
385:     h5 {
386:       font-family: 'Geist Mono', monospace; font-size: 10.5px;
387:       font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase;
388:       color: var(--n8); margin-top: 14px; break-after: avoid;
389:     }
390:     h6 {
391:       font-size: 13px; font-weight: 700; font-style: italic;
392:       color: var(--n6); margin-top: 12px; break-after: avoid;
393:     }
394:
395:     /* Plus-sign highlight list (for features, benefits) */
396:     .highlight-list {
397:       margin: 8px 0 14px 0;
398:       padding: 0;
399:       list-style: none;
400:       font-size: 15px;
401:       line-height: 1.65;
402:     }
403:
404:     .highlight-list li {
405:       padding-left: 18px;
406:       position: relative;
407:       margin-bottom: 5px;
408:     }
409:
410:     .highlight-list li::before {
411:       content: '+';
412:       position: absolute;
413:       left: 0;
414:       top: 0;
415:       font-weight: 700;
416:       color: var(--rm-blue);
417:       font-size: 16px;
418:     }
419:
420:     /* Ordered list (canonical): bold RM Blue numeral at level 1, then
421:        subtle lowercase letters at level 2, and smaller lowercase roman
422:        numerals at level 3. Classical legal/academic outline pattern. */
423:     .numbered-list, ol.body-list {
424:       margin: 8px 0 14px 0;
425:       padding: 0;
426:       list-style: none;
427:       counter-reset: l1;
428:       font-size: 15px;
429:       line-height: 1.65;
430:     }
431:     .numbered-list li, ol.body-list li {
432:       padding-left: 20px;
433:       position: relative;
434:       margin-bottom: 5px;
435:     }
436:     .numbered-list > li, ol.body-list > li {
437:       counter-increment: l1;
438:     }
439:     .numbered-list > li::before, ol.body-list > li::before {
440:       content: counter(l1);
441:       position: absolute;
442:       left: 0;
443:       top: -2px;
444:       font-weight: 700;
445:       color: var(--rm-blue);
446:       font-size: 18px;
447:       letter-spacing: -0.2px;
448:     }
449:     .numbered-list ol, ol.body-list ol {
450:       counter-reset: l2;
451:       padding-left: 2px;
452:       margin-top: 4px;
453:     }
454:     .numbered-list ol > li, ol.body-list ol > li {
455:       padding-left: 16px;
456:       counter-increment: l2;
457:       font-size: 14px;
458:       color: var(--n8);
459:     }
460:     .numbered-list ol > li::before, ol.body-list ol > li::before {
461:       content: counter(l2, lower-alpha) ".";
462:       position: absolute;
463:       left: 0;
464:       top: 0;
465:       font-family: 'Geist Mono', monospace;
466:       font-size: 11.5px;
467:       color: var(--dark-blue-green);
468:       font-weight: 500;
469:       letter-spacing: 0.02em;
470:     }
471:     .numbered-list ol ol, ol.body-list ol ol {
472:       counter-reset: l3;
473:     }
474:     .numbered-list ol ol > li, ol.body-list ol ol > li {
475:       padding-left: 18px;
476:       counter-increment: l3;
477:       font-size: 13px;
478:       color: var(--n7);
479:     }
480:     .numbered-list ol ol > li::before, ol.body-list ol ol > li::before {
481:       content: counter(l3, lower-roman) ".";
482:       position: absolute;
483:       left: 0;
484:       top: 1px;
485:       font-family: 'Geist Mono', monospace;
486:       font-size: 10.5px;
487:       color: var(--n6);
488:       font-weight: 500;
489:       letter-spacing: 0.02em;
490:     }
491:
492:     /* Bold-lead list (numbered, first sentence bold) */
493:     .bold-lead-list {
494:       margin: 8px 0 14px 0;
495:       padding: 0;
496:       list-style: none;
497:       counter-reset: bl-counter;
498:       font-size: 15px;
499:       line-height: 1.65;
500:     }
501:
502:     .bold-lead-list li {
503:       padding-left: 24px;
504:       position: relative;
505:       margin-bottom: 10px;
506:       counter-increment: bl-counter;
507:     }
508:
509:     .bold-lead-list li::before {
510:       content: counter(bl-counter) ".";
511:       position: absolute;
512:       left: 0;
513:       top: 0;
514:       font-weight: 700;
515:       color: var(--rm-blue);
516:     }
517:
518:     /* ── Section separators ── */
519:     .section-rule {
520:       border: none;
521:       border-top: 1px solid var(--rule-gray);
522:       margin: 28px 0;
523:     }
524:
525:     .part-separator { display: none; }
526:     .page-break-before { break-before: page; }
527:
528:     /* ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
529:        CALLOUT BOXES
530:        ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */
531:
532:     .exercise-box {
533:       background: var(--callout-bg);
534:       border-left: 3px solid var(--rm-blue);
535:       padding: 16px 20px;
536:       margin: 16px 0 20px 0;
537:       border-radius: 0 4px 4px 0;
538:       break-inside: avoid;
539:     }
540:
541:     .exercise-box .exercise-label {
542:       font-family: 'Geist Mono', monospace;
543:       font-size: 11px;
544:       font-weight: 400;
545:       letter-spacing: 0.06em;
546:       text-transform: uppercase;
547:       color: var(--rm-blue);
548:       margin-bottom: 4px;
549:     }
550:
551:     .exercise-box .exercise-title {
552:       font-weight: 700;
553:       font-size: 17px;
554:       color: var(--rm-dark-blue);
555:       margin-bottom: 8px;
556:     }
557:
558:     .exercise-box .exercise-body {
559:       font-size: 14px;
560:       line-height: 1.6;
561:       color: var(--text);
562:     }
563:
564:     .exercise-box .exercise-body p { margin-bottom: 6px; }
565:     .exercise-box .exercise-body ul { margin: 6px 0 8px 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; }
566:     .exercise-box .exercise-body ul li { padding-left: 16px; position: relative; margin-bottom: 4px; }
567:     .exercise-box .exercise-body ul li::before {
568:       content: ''; position: absolute; left: 0; top: 6px;
569:       width: 5px; height: 5px; background: var(--rm-blue); border-radius: 1px;
570:     }
571:
572:     .note-box {
573:       background: #FFF9E6;
574:       border-left: 3px solid var(--orange);
575:       padding: 14px 18px;
576:       margin: 16px 0;
577:       border-radius: 0 4px 4px 0;
578:       font-size: 14px;
579:       line-height: 1.6;
580:       break-inside: avoid;
581:     }
582:
583:     .note-box .note-title {
584:       font-weight: 700;
585:       font-size: 15px;
586:       color: var(--rm-dark-blue);
587:       margin-bottom: 4px;
588:     }
589:
590:     .info-box {
591:       background: #EDF4FC;
592:       border-left: 3px solid var(--rm-blue);
593:       padding: 14px 18px;
594:       margin: 16px 0;
595:       border-radius: 0 4px 4px 0;
596:       font-size: 14px;
597:       line-height: 1.6;
598:       break-inside: avoid;
599:     }
600:
601:     .info-box .info-title {
602:       font-weight: 700;
603:       font-size: 15px;
604:       color: var(--rm-dark-blue);
605:       margin-bottom: 4px;
606:     }
607:
608:     .warning-box {
609:       background: #FDF2F2;
610:       border-left: 3px solid #D4605A;
611:       padding: 14px 18px;
612:       margin: 16px 0;
613:       border-radius: 0 4px 4px 0;
614:       font-size: 14px;
615:       line-height: 1.6;
616:       break-inside: avoid;
617:     }
618:
619:     .warning-box .warning-title {
620:       font-weight: 700;
621:       font-size: 15px;
622:       color: #D4605A;
623:       margin-bottom: 4px;
624:     }

626:     /* ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
627:        CODE AND PROMPTS
628:        ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */
629:     .prompt-text {
630:       font-family: 'Geist Mono', monospace;
631:       font-size: 12.5px;
632:       background: #FFFFFF;
633:       border: 1px solid var(--rule-gray);
634:       border-radius: 4px;
635:       padding: 10px 14px;
636:       margin: 8px 0;
637:       line-height: 1.5;
638:       color: var(--text);
639:       display: block;
640:       white-space: pre-wrap;
641:     }

643:     /* ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
644:        DATA TABLES
645:        ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */
646:     .quick-ref-table {
647:       width: 100%;
648:       border-collapse: collapse;
649:       margin: 16px 0;
650:       font-size: 14px;
651:     }
652:
653:     .quick-ref-table th {
654:       text-align: left;
655:       font-weight: 700;
656:       color: var(--rm-dark-blue);
657:       border-bottom: 2px solid var(--rm-blue);
658:       padding: 8px 12px;
659:     }
660:
661:     .quick-ref-table td {
662:       border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule-gray);
663:       padding: 8px 12px;
664:       vertical-align: top;
665:     }
666:
667:     .quick-ref-table .metric-value {
668:       text-align: right;
669:       font-family: 'Geist Mono', monospace;
670:       font-size: 13px;
671:     }
672:
673:     /* Service table (type + bulleted services) */
674:     .service-table {
675:       width: 100%;
676:       border-collapse: collapse;
677:       margin: 16px 0;
678:       font-size: 14px;
679:     }
680:
681:     .service-table th {
682:       text-align: left;
683:       font-weight: 700;
684:       color: var(--rm-dark-blue);
685:       border-bottom: 2px solid var(--rm-blue);
686:       padding: 8px 12px;
687:     }
688:
689:     .service-table td {
690:       border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule-gray);
691:       padding: 8px 12px;
692:       vertical-align: top;
693:     }
694:
695:     .service-table .service-type {
696:       font-weight: 700;
697:       color: var(--rm-dark-blue);
698:       width: 30%;
699:     }
700:
701:     .service-table ul {
702:       margin: 0 0 0 16px;
703:       padding: 0;
704:       list-style: none;
705:     }
706:
707:     .service-table ul li {
708:       padding-left: 14px;
709:       position: relative;
710:       margin-bottom: 3px;
711:     }
712:
713:     .service-table ul li::before {
714:       content: '';
715:       position: absolute;
716:       left: 0;
717:       top: 6px;
718:       width: 4px;
719:       height: 4px;
720:       background: var(--rm-blue);
721:       border-radius: 1px;
722:     }
723:
724:     /* ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
725:        COMPARISON COMPONENTS
726:        ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */
727:     .two-col { display: flex; gap: 16px; margin: 12px 0 20px 0; }
728:     .two-col-card { flex: 1; border-radius: 4px; padding: 14px 18px; }
729:     .two-col-card-title { font-weight: 700; font-size: 14px; margin-bottom: 2px; color: var(--rm-dark-blue); }
730:     .two-col-card-subtitle {
731:       font-family: 'Geist Mono', monospace; font-size: 11px;
732:       text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.04em; margin-bottom: 8px;
733:     }
734:     .two-col-card ul { margin: 0; padding: 0; font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.6; list-style: none; }
735:     .two-col-card ul li { padding-left: 14px; position: relative; margin-bottom: 3px; }
736:     .two-col-card ul li::before {
737:       content: ''; position: absolute; left: 0; top: 6px;
738:       width: 4px; height: 4px; border-radius: 1px;
739:     }

741:     /* ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
742:        VISUAL COMPONENTS
743:        ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */
744:
745:     .stat-callout {
746:       text-align: center;
747:       margin: 20px 0;
748:     }
749:
750:     .stat-callout .stat-number {

822:
823:     /* ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
824:        PAGED.JS: Preview-only styles (screen only, not printed)
825:        ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ */
826:     @media screen, pagedjs-ignore {
827:       html { background: #cacaca; }
828:       .pagedjs_pages {
829:         display: flex;
830:         flex-direction: column;
831:         align-items: center;
832:         width: auto;
833:         padding: 40px 0;

835:       }
836:       .pagedjs_page {
837:         background: white;
838:         box-shadow: 0 2px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.25), 0 0 0 1px rgba(0,0,0,0.08);
839:         margin: 0;
840:       }
841:     }

847:

849: </head>
850: <body>
851:

60:     .token-table code { background: #F5F5F5; padding: 2px 6px; border-radius: 3px; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'SF Mono', 'Fira Code', monospace; }
61:     .match  { color: #2E7D32; font-weight: 600; font-size: 11px; }
62:     .close  { color: #E65100; font-weight: 600; font-size: 11px; }
63:     .miss   { color: #C62828; font-weight: 600; font-size: 11px; }
64:     .bar-row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; padding: 8px 0; border-bottom: 1px solid #F0F0F0; }
65:     .bar-label { font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; min-width: 240px; font-family: 'SF Mono', 'Fira Code', monospace; color: #181A18; }
66:     .bar-track { flex: 1; height: 18px; background: #F0F0F0; border-radius: 4px; overflow: hidden; }
67:     .bar-fill { height: 100%; border-radius: 4px; }
68:     .bar-fill.high   { background: linear-gradient(90deg, #F44336, #C62828); }
69:     .bar-fill.medium { background: linear-gradient(90deg, #FFA726, #E65100); }
70:     .bar-fill.low    { background: linear-gradient(90deg, #66BB6A, #2E7D32); }
71:     .bar-count { font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; min-width: 30px; text-align: right; color: #545454; }
72:     .findings-table { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 14px; margin-top: 16px; }
73:     .findings-table th { background: #F5F5F5; font-weight: 700; text-align: left; padding: 10px 14px; border: 1px solid #E0E0E0; font-size: 12px; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #545454; }
74:     .findings-table td { padding: 12px 14px; border: 1px solid #E0E0E0; color: #181A18; height: 44px; }
75:     .findings-table tr:nth-child(even) td { background: #FAFAFA; }
76:     .severity-badge { font-size: 10px; font-weight: 700; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 10px; color: white; display: inline-block; }
77:     .badge-critical { background: #C62828; }
78:     .badge-high     { background: #E65100; }
79:     .badge-medium   { background: #1565C0; }
80:     .badge-pattern  { background: #6A1B9A; }
81:     .comp-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 10px; margin-top: 12px; }
82:     .comp-card { background: white; border: 1px solid #E0E0E0; border-radius: 8px; padding: 14px 16px; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; }
83:     .comp-from   { font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; color: #C62828; min-width: 140px; font-family: 'SF Mono', monospace; }
84:     .comp-arrow  { color: #3A70B3; font-size: 16px; flex-shrink: 0; }
85:     .comp-to     { font-size: 13px; font-weight: 600; color: #2E7D32; }
86:     .comp-tokens { font-size: 11px; color: #888; }
87:     .doc-footer { margin-top: 80px; padding-top: 24px; border-top: 1px solid #E0E0E0; font-size: 12px; color: #999; line-height: 1.8; }
88:     hr { border: none; border-top: 1px solid #E0E0E0; margin: 0 0 56px 0; }
89:     h3.table-label { font-size: 17px; font-weight: 700; color: #181A18; margin: 24px 0 8px; }
90:   </style>
91: </head>
92: <body>
93: <div class="page">
94:
95:   <span class="eyebrow">UX/UI Audit</span>
96:   <h1 class="doc-title">BetaNXT Issuer Portal</h1>
97:
98:   <div class="meta-fields">
99:     <p><strong>Product being audited:</strong> BetaNXT Issuer Portal</p>
100:     <p><strong>Auditor(s):</strong> opencode / ux-audit skill</p>
101:     <p><strong>Date:</strong> May 18, 2026</p>
102:     <p><strong>Tech stack:</strong> Next.js 16 + React 19 + TypeScript, MUI v7, CSS</p>
103:     <p><strong>Design system target:</strong> @rolemodel/betanxt-design-system v1.1.1</p>
104:     <p><strong>Live URL:</strong> http://localhost:3000</p>
105:     <p><strong>Figma file:</strong> Not linked</p>

108:   <div class="callout">
109:     <div class="callout-title">How to use this document:</div>
110:     <p>Work through each section during the heuristic walkthrough. For each item, check it off when evaluated and record observations below the section. Rate severity:</p>
111:     <div class="severity-row">
112:       <div class="severity-item"><div class="severity-dot dot-green"></div> Holding up well</div>
113:       <div class="severity-item"><div class="severity-dot dot-yellow"></div> Opportunity</div>
114:       <div class="severity-item"><div class="severity-dot dot-red"></div> Significant gap</div>
115:     </div>
116:     <p class="callout-note">Not every item will apply to every product — use judgment. The goal is a rich findings list, not a complete score. Code scan data (hardcoded values, token mapping) is appended at the end.</p>
117:   </div>
118:
119:   <div class="exec-summary">
120:     <div class="exec-title">Executive Summary</div>
121:     <div class="stat-row">
122:       <div class="stat-box">
123:         <div class="stat-num">441</div>
124:         <div class="stat-label">Hardcoded color refs</div>
125:       </div>
126:       <div class="stat-box">
127:         <div class="stat-num">7</div>
128:         <div class="stat-label">WCAG contrast risks</div>
129:       </div>
130:       <div class="stat-box">
131:         <div class="stat-num">32</div>
132:         <div class="stat-label">Total findings</div>
133:       </div>
134:       <div class="stat-box">
135:         <div class="stat-num">24/52</div>
136:         <div class="stat-label">Colors exact-match tokens</div>
137:       </div>
138:     </div>
139:     <div class="exec-verdict">The BetaNXT Issuer Portal is a mature, MUI-based application with a solid design system foundation (@rolemodel/betanxt-design-system). The architecture is sound — CSS variables are used correctly in stylesheets, MUI components are well-customized, and there's a shared EmptyState, SkeletonTable, and Snackbar pattern. The single most important recommendation is to eliminate the 10 instances of native `alert()` calls and replace them with MUI Snackbar/toast patterns, as these block the main thread and provide no accessibility hooks. The effort to migrate hardcoded colors in PDF export utilities and the signature-maker.css to design tokens is moderate (~2-3 days) and would significantly improve maintainability.</div>
140:   </div>
141:
142:   <!-- SECTION 1 -->
143:   <div class="section">
144:     <div class="section-header">
145:       <h2 class="section-title">Section 1: First Impressions &amp; Visual Coherence</h2>
146:     </div>
147:     <p class="section-intro">What a user feels in the first 30 seconds — and whether the product looks and feels like one thing.</p>
148:     <div class="checklist">
149:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Does the product make a strong first impression? Is the purpose immediately clear? Does it feel trustworthy and intentional?</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>Aesthetic-Usability Effect: Users perceive aesthetically pleasing design as more usable.</p></div><div class="check-finding opportunity">[S1-1] <strong>Opportunity.</strong> 76 unique hardcoded hex colors across 25+ files create visual drift. MUI-based architecture is solid, but PDF export utilities and signature-maker.css use colors disconnected from the theme system. (P)</div></div>
150:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Is the visual language consistent throughout? Check button styles, typography, color usage, spacing, and iconography across multiple screens.</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>Law of Similarity / Law of Uniform Connectedness: Inconsistent visual treatment signals inconsistent relationships.</p></div><div class="check-finding gap">[S1-2] <strong>Gap.</strong> #EBB322 hardcoded in StatusChip.tsx:189 instead of using var(--mui-palette-gold-500). signature-maker.css uses #053f5a, #D3D3D3, #000 hardcoded — all have exact token equivalents. 58 hardcoded pixel values in inline styles. (H)</div></div>
151:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Does the brand come through clearly?</label></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S1-3] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> Multi-tenant brand system with 50+ client configs in brandConfig.ts. createClientTheme() properly merges brand colors with base theme. ClientAppSwitcher enables cross-client navigation. (Pass)</div></div>
152:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Is there visual hierarchy on key screens?</label></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S1-4] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> MUI typography scale managed by betanxt-design-system. Only 10 hardcoded font-size values, all in PDF exports — not in the main UI. Phase-based layout system provides clear content hierarchy. (Pass)</div></div>
153:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Is the color system doing meaningful work?</label></div><div class="check-finding opportunity">[S1-5] <strong>Opportunity.</strong> MUI CSS variables used correctly in stylesheets (var(--mui-palette-*), var(--mui-shadows-*)). But 441 total hardcoded color references undermine the system. 24 of 52 unique colors have exact token matches available. (P)</div></div>
154:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Does the typography scale feel intentional?</label></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S1-6] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> baseTypography imported from betanxt-design-system/themes/base/typography. dataCell, dataHeader, caption variants defined in theme overrides. No arbitrary font-size values in the main UI. (Pass)</div></div>
155:     </div>
156:     <span class="observations-label">Observations:</span>
157:     <div class="observations-area">[S1-1] <strong>Hardcoded color drift across components.</strong> 76 unique hardcoded hex colors found across 25+ files. While many are in the dynamic brandConfig.ts (expected for multi-tenant branding), significant drift exists in PDF export utilities, StatusChip (#EBB322 hardcoded at issuer-portal/components/ui/StatusChip.tsx:189), and signature-maker.css (#053f5a, #D3D3D3). (P)
158: [S1-2] <strong>Typography scale is MUI-managed — good.</strong> The design system provides typography via baseTypography from betanxt-design-system. Only 10 hardcoded font-size values found, all in PDF export utilities and signature-maker.css, not in the main UI. (Holding up well)
159: [S1-3] <strong>Brand system is multi-tenant by design.</strong> 50+ client brand configs in brandConfig.ts with dynamic primaryColor/secondaryColor. This is intentional architecture, not a drift issue. Theme creation via createClientTheme() properly merges brand colors with the base theme. (Holding up well)</div>
160:   </div>
161:
162:   <!-- SECTION 2 -->
163:   <div class="section">
164:     <div class="section-header">
165:       <h2 class="section-title">Section 2: Navigation &amp; Wayfinding</h2>
166:     </div>
167:     <p class="section-intro">Can users find what they need, understand where they are, and get back if they get lost?</p>
168:     <div class="checklist">
169:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Is the navigation structure predictable?</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>Jakob's Law: Users expect your product to work like others they know.</p></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S2-1] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> EventTabs provides scrollable meeting navigation with aria-labeled arrows. AppBar follows standard web conventions with logo, tabs, notifications, and profile. PhaseDrawer organizes content by workflow stage. (Pass)</div></div>
170:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Do users always know where they are?</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>Users shouldn't have to remember where they are.</p></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S2-2] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> PageTitle.tsx includes breadcrumb navigation with aria-label="breadcrumb". PhaseDrawer shows current phase number. EventTabs highlight active meeting. (Pass)</div></div>
171:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Are navigation labels clear and in plain language?</label></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S2-3] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> Navigation labels use plain language: "Scroll meetings left/right", "Add new task", "Share calendar", "Enter fullscreen". No internal jargon detected in aria-labels. (Pass)</div></div>
172:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Is the depth of navigation appropriate?</label></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S2-4] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> Route structure: /[clientTicker]/meeting/[meetingId]/[section] — 3 levels max. PhaseDrawer provides in-context navigation within meetings. Most content reachable in ≤3 clicks. (Pass)</div></div>
173:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Does the navigation work on mobile?</label></div><div class="check-finding opportunity">[S2-5] <strong>Opportunity.</strong> useMediaQuery(theme.breakpoints.down('md')) used in EventTabs, PhaseDrawer, MonthView, NumberCounter. But no skip-nav link means mobile keyboard users must tab through full AppBar. (M)</div></div>
174:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Are there dead ends?</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>Users need a clearly marked "emergency exit".</p></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S2-6] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> EmptyState component used in 10+ locations with clear CTAs. Dialogs have close buttons with aria-label. PhaseDrawer has "Close upload view and return to overview" button. (Pass)</div></div>
175:     </div>
176:     <span class="observations-label">Observations:</span>
177:     <div class="observations-area">[S2-1] <strong>EventTabs provides meeting navigation with scroll arrows.</strong> EventTabs.tsx implements left/right scroll buttons with aria-labels ("Scroll meetings left/right"). The component uses useMediaQuery for mobile detection at md breakpoint. (Holding up well)
178: [S2-2] <strong>PageTitle includes breadcrumb navigation.</strong> PageTitle.tsx has aria-label="breadcrumb", providing wayfinding context. (Holding up well)
179: [S2-3] <strong>ClientAppSwitcher enables cross-client navigation.</strong> The AppBar includes a ClientAppSwitcher component with role="complementary" at issuer-portal/components/Navigation/AppBar.tsx:160. (Holding up well)
180: [S2-4] <strong>Phase-based drawer navigation.</strong> PhaseDrawer uses useMediaQuery for mobile (md breakpoint) and provides phase-based content organization with aria-label="Loading phase data" and role="region" for each phase. (Holding up well)</div>
181:   </div>
182:
183:   <!-- SECTION 3 -->
184:   <div class="section">
185:     <div class="section-header">
186:       <h2 class="section-title">Section 3: Cognitive Load &amp; Complexity</h2>
187:     </div>
188:     <p class="section-intro">How hard is the product making users think?</p>
189:     <div class="checklist">
190:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Are screens trying to do too much?</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>Hick's Law / Miller's Law: Decision time increases with complexity.</p></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S3-1] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> Phase-based workflow breaks complex meeting management into digestible stages. PhaseDrawer organizes content by workflow step. SkeletonTable used consistently to reduce visual load during loading. (Pass)</div></div>
191:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Is information chunked effectively?</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>Law of Common Region / Proximity: Grouping reduces cognitive effort.</p></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S3-2] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> Card-based layout (MUI Card) groups related information. MeetingInformationCard, VotingSharesCard, MeetingRolesCard each handle one concern. Tabulation uses separate tables for proposals and positions. (Pass)</div></div>
192:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Are forms as simple as they can be?</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>Occam's Razor: Every extra field is a cost to the user.</p></div><div class="check-finding opportunity">[S3-3] <strong>Opportunity.</strong> FileUploadDialog has clear flow but no field-level validation feedback visible in code. Form utilities (planFileRequestForm, transferAgentRequestForm) use hardcoded colors (#969696, #C8C8C8, #F0F0F0) suggesting custom form styling outside MUI. (M)</div></div>
193:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Does the UI surface meaningful defaults?</label></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S3-4] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> EmptyState provides default content when no data exists. SkeletonTable shows structural placeholder during loading. MUI components have sensible defaults (elevation, spacing, typography). (Pass)</div></div>
194:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Is the language plain and direct?</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>Speak the user's language, not the system's.</p></div><div class="check-finding opportunity">[S3-5] <strong>Opportunity.</strong> Error messages in alert() calls are human-readable ("Failed to download document. Please try again.") but the alert() pattern itself is jarring. TabulationReportCard uses "Unable to generate report. Meeting data is not available." — clear but could suggest next steps. (M)</div></div>
195:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Are there progress indicators for multi-step processes?</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>Goal-Gradient Effect / Zeigarnik Effect.</p></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S3-6] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> PhaseDrawer with phase-based progress. LinearProgress with custom phase colors (theme.ts:703-756). Meeting phases clearly numbered and labeled. CircularProgress used for async operations. (Pass)</div></div>
196:     </div>
197:     <span class="observations-label">Observations:</span>
198:     <div class="observations-area">[S3-1] <strong>Phase-based progress system.</strong> The PhaseDrawer and PhaseContext provide a structured multi-step workflow with progress tracking. LinearProgress supports custom phase colors via CSS variables (theme.ts:703-756). (Holding up well)
199: [S3-2] <strong>Skeleton loading states reduce perceived complexity.</strong> SkeletonTable is used consistently across DocumentsSection, VotingTabulationTable, QuorumPerformanceTable, and PastMeetingsTable. ChartSkeleton used on reporting pages. (Holding up well)
200: [S3-3] <strong>EmptyState component used consistently.</strong> Found in 10+ locations including reports, meetings, documents, guests, agenda, and digital shareholder meeting pages. Provides consistent empty-state UX. (Holding up well)</div>
201:   </div>
202:
203:   <!-- SECTION 4 -->
204:   <div class="section">
205:     <div class="section-header">
206:       <h2 class="section-title">Section 4: Key Flows &amp; Task Completion</h2>
207:     </div>
208:     <p class="section-intro">Walk through the most critical user journeys.</p>
209:     <div class="tasks-block">
210:       <p>Core tasks being evaluated:</p>
211:       Review and manage meeting documents (upload, view, comment)<br>
212:       Track voting tabulation and generate reports<br>
213:       Manage meeting phases and timelines
214:     </div>
215:     <div class="checklist">
216:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Is the entry point obvious?</label></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S4-1] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> EventTabs provide clear meeting navigation entry. PhaseDrawer shows available phases with content. DocumentsSection has clear upload button. (Pass)</div></div>
217:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Are calls to action clear and appropriately sized?</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>Fitts's Law: Target size and distance affect accuracy.</p></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S4-2] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> MUI Button component used throughout with variant hierarchy (contained > outlined > text). FileUploadDialog has clear submit button with loading state. Export buttons use MUI Button with dropdown menus. (Pass)</div></div>
218:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Does the flow match the user's mental model?</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>When product structure doesn't match user thinking, errors increase.</p></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S4-3] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> Phase-based workflow mirrors real meeting planning process (setup → documents → mailing → voting → tabulation → reporting). MeetingInformationCard, DocumentsSection, VotingTabulation follow natural meeting lifecycle. (Pass)</div></div>
219:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Are there unnecessary interruptions or confirmation steps?</label></div><div class="check-finding gap">[S4-4] <strong>Gap.</strong> No confirmation dialogs found for delete operations. SecureFileTransferTable has "Delete file" button with no visible confirmation step. VotingSharesCard has alert(`Confirm action for ${label}`) at line 37 — a placeholder, not a real confirmation. (H)</div></div>
220:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Are error states handled gracefully?</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>Error messages should be plain language, identify the problem, suggest a solution.</p></div><div class="check-finding gap">[S4-5] <strong>Gap.</strong> 10 native alert() calls across the codebase: DocumentViewer.tsx (4), TabulationReportCard.tsx (1), DocumentSiteCard.tsx (1), DSMParticipants.tsx (1), broadridgeFormHandler.tsx (1), VotingSharesCard.tsx (1), TaskActions.tsx (1). These are modal-blocking, non-dismissable by Escape, and provide no accessibility hooks. (C) — replace with MUI Snackbar.</div></div>
221:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Does the product handle edge cases?</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>Postel's Law: Gracefully handle unexpected input.</p></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S4-6] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> EmptyState component used in 10+ locations. SkeletonTable for loading states. Error boundaries in PDF viewer (DocumentViewer.tsx:260). Form validation in FileUploadDialog. (Pass)</div></div>
222:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">What is the peak moment and ending of each flow?</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>Peak-End Rule: Users judge by the most intense moment and the end.</p></div><div class="check-finding opportunity">[S4-7] <strong>Opportunity.</strong> File upload flow ends with "Submit" button changing to "Uploading..." — good feedback. But success confirmation uses alert() instead of a celebratory Snackbar. Document download errors end with alert("Failed to download document. Please try again.") — functional but not reassuring. (M)</div></div>
223:     </div>
224:     <span class="observations-label">Observations:</span>
225:     <div class="observations-area">[S4-1] <strong>Native alert() calls block task flows.</strong> Found 10 instances of native `alert()` across the codebase: DocumentViewer.tsx (4), TabulationReportCard.tsx (1), DocumentSiteCard.tsx (1), DSMParticipants.tsx (1), broadridgeFormHandler.tsx (1), VotingSharesCard.tsx (1), TaskActions.tsx (1). These are modal-blocking, non-dismissable by keyboard escape, and provide no accessibility hooks. (C) — replace with MUI Snackbar.
226: [S4-2] <strong>FileUploadDialog provides clear upload flow.</strong> FileUploadDialog.tsx has proper disabled states during upload, clear submit button text changes ("Uploading..." vs "Submit"), and a close button with aria-label. (Holding up well)
227: [S4-3] <strong>DocumentViewer has download error handling.</strong> Multiple alert() calls for download failures (DocumentViewer.tsx:954, 987, 1009, 1107) — see S4-1. The error messages are human-readable but use the wrong pattern.</div>
228:   </div>
229:
230:   <!-- SECTION 5 -->
231:   <div class="section">
232:     <div class="section-header">
233:       <h2 class="section-title">Section 5: Feedback &amp; System Communication</h2>
234:     </div>
235:     <p class="section-intro">Does the product keep users informed and in control?</p>
236:     <div class="checklist">
237:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Does the product acknowledge user actions?</label></div><div class="check-description"><div class="spacer"></div><p>Visibility of System Status / Doherty Threshold.</p></div><div class="check-finding gap">[S5-1] <strong>Gap.</strong> PhaseDrawer has snackbar (snackbarMessage, snackbarOpen at PhaseDrawer.tsx:201-202) but DocumentViewer and other components use alert() instead. Inconsistent feedback patterns mean users get different responses depending on which flow they're in. (H)</div></div>
238:       <div class="check-item"><div class="check-row"><input type="checkbox" checked><label class="check-label">Are loading states handled?</label></div><div class="check-finding pass">[S5-2] <strong>Holding up well.</strong> 476 loading-related matches.
